name: The Metanarrative: Creation, Fall, Redemption, Restoration

objectives.text: Identify that God made the world and everything in it and called it very good
Retell how Adam and Eve disobeyed God in the garden and name what happened as a result
Recall that God sent Jesus to rescue sinners
Describe what Scripture says God will do when he makes all things new
Summarize the Bible's big story using the four parts of creation, fall, redemption, and restoration
Describe how God made people in his image and gave them work to do in his good creation
Explain from Genesis 3 and Romans 5 why all people need a Rescuer
Compare the Garden of Eden with the New Jerusalem to show how the end of the story answers its beginning
Explain how the Fall broke humanity's relationship with God, with one another, and with the rest of creation
Explain how Scripture uses the promise of final restoration to direct believers in how to respond to suffering
Analyze how individual Bible narratives fit within the larger arc of creation, fall, redemption, and restoration
Interpret Genesis 3:15 as the first promise of redemption and trace its fulfillment in Christ
Analyze examples of present-day brokenness in people, society, and nature as consequences of the Fall
Explain how God's single plan of redemption unfolds consistently from Genesis to Revelation
Explain why the person and work of Christ stand at the center of the redemption movement of the biblical story
Construct an annotated timeline of the biblical metanarrative that places key events and supporting texts in each of the four movements
Distinguish the biblical hope of a restored physical creation from views that picture salvation as escape from the material world
Evaluate the accounts other worldviews give of origin, problem, solution, and destiny against the biblical metanarrative
Defend the Reformed position that a historical Fall is necessary to the logic of the gospel
Analyze how the Westminster Confession and Heidelberg Catechism organize their teaching around the movements of the biblical story
Develop a written explanation of how the Reformed tradition understands the Christian's calling in the present age within the four-part story

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (good creation, the Fall, Jesus the Rescuer, all things new, four-part summary, need for a Rescuer, Eden and New Jerusalem, stories within the arc, Genesis 3:15, present brokenness, consistency of God's plan, timeline, worldview evaluation, historical Fall). Reframed the feelings-based 'bad day' objective as explaining how Scripture directs believers in suffering. Reframed the vague 'believer's role' synthesis as an explanation of the Reformed view of calling. Added image-bearing and work in creation, the relational effects of the Fall, Christ at the center of redemption, a restored physical creation versus escape views, and how the confessions organize the story. Left covenant structure, typology, and already/not yet to sibling sub-topics. Replaced whole-chapter citations with verse ranges and added catechism and confession anchors where they state the doctrine.
